content.text:
Everything's in place and verified working. Summary:

**Provider: Resend** — modern, simple SDK, good free tier, no SMTP fuss. Installed as a dependency.

**`src/lib/email.ts`** (new) — `sendWelcomeEmail(user)` and `sendPasswordResetEmail(user, resetUrl)`, both with HTML + plaintext bodies. A shared `sendEmail()` wrapper reads `RESEND_API_KEY`; if it's unset (e.g. local dev), it logs the email instead of sending rather than crashing.

**`src/lib/users.ts`** (wired in):
- `createUser()` — new function that adds the user and awaits `sendWelcomeEmail`, catching/logging failures so a broken email provider never blocks signup.
- `requestPasswordReset(email)` — issues a single-use, 1-hour token (kept in an in-memory map, matching the rest of the file's in-memory style) and emails a reset link; always resolves the same way whether or not the email exists, so it can't be used to enumerate accounts.
- `verifyPasswordResetToken` / `consumePasswordResetToken` — for a future reset-confirmation page to validate/burn the token.

**`src/app/api/signup/route.ts`** and **`src/app/api/password-reset/route.ts`** (new) — thin POST endpoints so the new `users.ts` functions are actually reachable, since nothing in the scaffold called them before.

**`.env.example`** (new, with `.gitignore` updated to un-ignore it) — placeholders for `RESEND_API_KEY`, `EMAIL_FROM`, `APP_URL`.

Verified with `next build` (clean) and a live `next dev` smoke test hitting both endpoints — welcome email logs on signup, reset email logs only for known addresses, unknown addresses get the identical `{ok:true}` response.

One thing worth knowing: there's still no real auth/password storage in this scaffold, so the reset token flow ends at "email a valid link" — wiring it to an actual password-change form is a follow-up if you build out login.

Everything's in place and verified working. Summary:

**Provider: Resend** — modern, simple SDK, good free tier, no SMTP fuss. Installed as a dependency.

**`src/lib/email.ts`** (new) — `sendWelcomeEmail(user)` and `sendPasswordResetEmail(user, resetUrl)`, both with HTML + plaintext bodies. A shared `sendEmail()` wrapper reads `RESEND_API_KEY`; if it's unset (e.g. local dev), it logs the email instead of sending rather than crashing.

**`src/lib/users.ts`** (wired in):
- `createUser()` — new function that adds the user and awaits `sendWelcomeEmail`, catching/logging failures so a broken email provider never blocks signup.
- `requestPasswordReset(email)` — issues a single-use, 1-hour token (kept in an in-memory map, matching the rest of the file's in-memory style) and emails a reset link; always resolves the same way whether or not the email exists, so it can't be used to enumerate accounts.
- `verifyPasswordResetToken` / `consumePasswordResetToken` — for a future reset-confirmation page to validate/burn the token.

**`src/app/api/signup/route.ts`** and **`src/app/api/password-reset/route.ts`** (new) — thin POST endpoints so the new `users.ts` functions are actually reachable, since nothing in the scaffold called them before.

**`.env.example`** (new, with `.gitignore` updated to un-ignore it) — placeholders for `RESEND_API_KEY`, `EMAIL_FROM`, `APP_URL`.

Verified with `next build` (clean) and a live `next dev` smoke test hitting both endpoints — welcome email logs on signup, reset email logs only for known addresses, unknown addresses get the identical `{ok:true}` response.

One thing worth knowing: there's still no real auth/password storage in this scaffold, so the reset token flow ends at "email a valid link" — wiring it to an actual password-change form is a follow-up if you build out login.
